title: Exploring Lift: Density, Speed, and Wing Area
learningObjectives: Calculate lift using the lift equation given lift coefficient, density, velocity, and wing area
Explain how lift varies with density, the square of velocity, and wing area
Describe the lift coefficient as collecting shape, inclination, viscosity, and compressibility effects

evidence.quote: Lift depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity, the air's viscosity and compressibility,
the surface area over which the air flows, the shape of the body, and the body's inclination to the flow.

explanations.text: Lift depends on air density, velocity squared, and wing surface area, plus body shape, inclination, viscosity, and compressibility.

evidence.quote: The lift equation states that lift L is equal to the lift coefficient Cl times the density rho

explanations.text: Lift equals the lift coefficient times density times half the velocity squared times wing area.

evidence.quote: For lift, this variable is called the lift coefficient, designated "Cl."
But, in general, this parameter is determined experimentally.

explanations.text: The lift coefficient collects shape, inclination, viscosity, and compressibility effects into one variable, often found by experiment.
